prompt: Propose a minimal architecture for a single-developer coding harness built on Pi. Keep orchestration and artifacts local; support multiple model providers, task-specific model tiers, bounded repair loops, independent reviews, and opt-in remote compute for heavy tests. Explain failure recovery and the smallest end-to-end implementation. Do not assume consumer subscriptions include API billing.

Independently critique this proposal: a local Pi-based coding harness dispatches models from multiple providers, chooses cheaper sufficient models for simple subtasks, uses isolated worktrees, and loops build/test/review/fix until acceptance or budget exhaustion. Identify the three most likely failure modes and propose testable mitigations. Distinguish subscription authentication from included billing. Do not assume agents agreeing proves correctness.

Write a short acceptance checklist for a local task router that selects models by minimum quality tier, supported reasoning effort, provider availability, and permitted billing mode. Include negative and concurrency tests.
